notes: Direct HTTP fetch, no blocking. 'Clearance' is a genuine top-level desktop mega-menu item (confirmed in raw HTML: Clearance, href /collections/clearance, plus an 'All Clearance' shop-all button) with three genuine site-defined level-3 children: Furniture Clearance (/collections/clearance-furniture), Lighting Clearance (/collections/clearance-lights), Home Accessories Clearance (/collections/home-accessories-clearance). All four headings confirmed by fetching each page directly (h1 text matches nav label exactly). SALE VS CLEARANCE CHECK: the site also has a separate top-level nav item 'Offers' (/pages/offers) listing temporary percent-off promotions (e.g. '20% off Anglepoise', '50% off Charingworth Cutlery', '30% off Villeroy & Boch') - this is a generic discount campaign, not clearance-style merchandising, and was excluded per brief Sec.3. Also found (via collections.json, 666 collections scanned across 3 pages, NOT linked in main nav) a 5th listing: 'Practically Perfect and Perfect Clearance' (/collections/practically-perfect-and-perfect-clearance) - h1 heading matches handle, real PLP. Its name and near-total overlap with the Clearance parent (78/79 = 99% of its products already sit in /collections/clearance) indicate a genuine ex-display/imperfect-condition clearance listing cross-cutting all three type categories (5/11 furniture, 68/99 lighting, 5/9 home-accessories items also appear in it) rather than a temporary sale or an alias of any single child - kept as its own leaf row, not flagged ambiguous since the clearance signal is unambiguous. QTY METHOD: exhaustive products.json pagination (limit=250, paged to empty), not the collections.json aggregate field (proven inflated for this site per the prior Home-Decor pass notes). COVERAGE CHECK for the parent grouping row: union of the 3 type-based children's unique product IDs covers 113/123 (92%) of the Clearance parent listing's own unique product IDs; the practically-perfect listing does not add coverage of the remaining 10 orphan items (they are also absent from it). Per the >=90%-coverage convention used in the prior Home-Decor pass for this same company, the parent is emitted as a null-qty grouping row (its own real qty is 123, exact, but is intentionally not used as a leaf qty to avoid double-counting against the children) with the 4 discovered listings as leaves; the 10 parent-only orphan items (8%) are a documented, non-fatal gap rather than a dropped category.
